standard_prerequisites.name: A regular sequence is Koszul regular and a Koszul regular sequence is H1-regular
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemmas \ref{lemma-regular-koszul-regular} and \ref{lemma-koszul-regular-H1-regular}, cited at proof lines 7885-7887
standard_prerequisites.use: Explain why the hypothesis of the lemma covers the classical cases of regular and Koszul regular sequences.

standard_prerequisites.name: The blowup algebra is the quotient of the polynomial ring over R by the ideal of torsion elements
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-affine-blowup-quotient-description}, cited at proof line 7894
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the identification of the blowup algebra to the absence of torsion by the first element.

standard_prerequisites.name: Koszul complexes are functorial under an isomorphism of the underlying modules, and Koszul regularity is preserved by flat base change
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-functorial} and Lemma \ref{lemma-koszul-regular-flat-base-change}, cited at proof lines 7915-7917
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfer H1-regularity from the given sequence to the transformed sequence in the polynomial ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex of a, ay_2 - a_2, ..., ay_r - a_r is the cone on multiplication by a on the Koszul complex of the remaining elements
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns vanishing of the first homology of the Koszul complex into injectivity of multiplication by a on the zeroth homology.

core_obligations: Reduce the claim to a-torsion freeness of the quotient ring by the affine blowup description (proof lines 7894-7895).
Claim that the sequence a, ay_2 - a_2, ..., ay_n - a_r is H1-regular in the polynomial ring (proof lines 7897-7899).
Exhibit an explicit change of coordinates making the Koszul differentials of the two sequences isomorphic, and apply functoriality and flat base change to prove the claim (proof lines 7900-7917).
Identify the Koszul complex of the transformed sequence as the cone on multiplication by a on the Koszul complex of the remaining elements (proof lines 7918-7919).
Use vanishing of the first homology to conclude that multiplication by a on the zeroth homology is injective, which is the required torsion freeness (proof lines 7920-7932).
proof_roadmap: Change coordinates and transfer H1-regularity (proof lines 7897-7917).
Identify the Koszul complex as a cone (proof lines 7918-7919).
Read off injectivity of multiplication by a (proof lines 7920-7932).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the blowup algebra of an ideal generated by an H1-regular sequence with an explicit quotient of a polynomial ring in the differences. The proof reduces to showing that this quotient has no torsion by the first element of the sequence, proves by an explicit change of coordinates that the transformed sequence is again H1-regular in the polynomial ring, and then reads the claimed torsion freeness off the long exact sequence of the Koszul complex: the Koszul complex of the transformed sequence is the cone on multiplication by the first element on the Koszul complex of the remaining elements, so vanishing of its first homology makes that multiplication injective on the zeroth homology. Both the coordinate change and the cone identification are written out.
